Puzzle 1216 Related to Puzzle 1212

Problems & Puzzles: Puzzles

Puzzle 1216 Related to Puzzle 1212
In this puzzle I will ask to insert a well defined string in-between each pair of consecutve digits of an integer p, according to the rule described in the sequence A381732, (Puzzle 1212). After making all the possible insertions in p, you will have a new integer q.

Example:

p=1693 (prime)

q= 123456789876543 (composite)

Here are the first nine p values such that p & q are both prime integers:

p | q

29 | 23456789

47 | 4567

73 | 76543

113 | 1123

239 | 23456789

269 | 23456789

353 | 34543

373 | 345676543

383 | 34567876543

In the table above I have used bold & blue characters only for these pairs (p, q) where both are palprimes

Q1. Find the first 20 pais (p, q) where both are palprimes

Q2. Send the largest q you can get where both p & q are palprimes.

During the week 11-17 Abril 2025, contributions came from Gennady Gusev, Paul Cleary, Michael Branicky, Emmanuel Vantieghem, Jeff Heleen, Giorgos Kalogeropoulos, Simon Cavegn

Q2

The largest p = q palprime is 111..111, the largest known prime RepUnit 8177207 digits long.

See https://www.elektrosoft.it/matematica/repunit/repunit.htm

The largest p = q palprime I could find myself:

Parallel processing happend to find two, both 75941 digits long.

Replace each .. with 37955 more zero's:

p = q = 110..0110101100100010011010110..011

p = q = 110..0110101001100011001010110..011
